open.what: The fact sheet leaves whole. From 0:06.0 its header strip sits half in frame, cut by the bottom edge, while the receipt is the subject.
open.basis: critic A stray (med); audit: sheet on screen 6.9 s.

open.what: Give the SO. stamp its own beat: the box stops typing while the stamp lands (0:02.5-0:05.0 both write at once).
open.basis: critic A two-focus (med). Eye check before building.

open.what: One copy of each receipt row during the hand-over at 0:07.7-0:08.1 (RECEIPT, TITLE, ARTIST, CHORUS OF MINDS are each drawn twice for 0.4 s); PAY ATTENTION reads once on the receipt (up to 4 ATTENTIONs at 0:06.0-0:08.1).

verse1.what: One copy of the Socrates line. Its typed words stay 6.2-7.4 s after they are sung (to 0:17.1) and at 0:17.2-0:20.3 every word of it is on screen twice. The handwriting is the keeper; the typed line leaves once the pen has caught up.
verse1.basis: audit dwell (5 words) + 11 repeat rows; critic A repeat (low).

verse1.what: Give three vanishing acts a cause on a cue: "years ago" (0:15.0), "THE" and "'S" of THE INK'S (0:18.5). Each is present in one frame and gone in the next while its neighbours stay.
verse1.basis: critic A exit x2 (med); film rule: exits land on cues.

verse1.what: One focus through 0:15.5-0:20.5: six text items in four typefaces at 0:15.5; small lyric far left against the large THE INK'S (0:16-0:18); the new line bottom-left while INK breaks into particles on the right (0:19); that line cut by the left edge at 0:20.5. Finish one event before the next starts and keep the sung line inside the frame.
verse1.basis: critic A two-focus x3 (high, med), stray (high).

verse1.what: The POCKET strip dims when it is written and leaves on the first downbeat of the class plate. It stays 6.5 s (0:24.5-0:31.0), the last 3.5 s after it has stopped being written, glowing under the new lines. Seam item with class.
verse1.basis: critic A dwell (high), two-focus at 0:28 (high); audit: board 7.8 s.

verse1.what: The ruled slab behind INK at 0:16.0 and its dark shadow copy of THE INK: give it a purpose the eye can see, or remove it.

class.what: The 2022 headline panel leaves one bar after the hole joke lands. The panel holds about 9 s (0:34-0:43), five of those seconds as "2022 THE ___ IS DEAD", and line 11 stays 6.0-8.1 s after it is sung.
class.basis: audit dwell (headline 8.8 s, 7 words); critic A dwell (med).

class.what: The second wall of WRITE IT FOR ME bubbles (0:35.5) differs from the first (0:31.5): fewer, changed or answered. Today it is the same 15 bubbles twice.

The essay reads once. In the wall at 0:36.9-0:41.4 "Industrial Revolution" is on screen up to 18 times, and the same text returns for 10.9 s in the next plate. One readable essay here; the other desks carry ruled lines. Build together with late-e01.
class.basis: audit repeat rows (up to 18 at once) + cross-plate texts; Idi's pinned note on late.

class.what: One THEY SAID and one IN YOUR HAND at 0:45-0:46 (boxed two and three times in a frame); the lone SAID box leaves with THEY (it stays 0:46.5-0:51.0 across three pictures).

Reading time: "Explain it to me" 0.5 s (needs 1.5), "THE ESSAY IS DEAD" 0.6 s (1.5), the worksheet header 1.4 s (1.8), "write me an essay on the industrial revolution" 1.9 s (2.5). Each gets its time, or shrinks to texture nobody is asked to read.
class.basis: audit reading rows (inventory gate: 0.25 s a word + 0.5 s).

class.what: Edges, check at 30 fps and fix what holds 0.5 s or more: "due tonight" cut by the left edge (0:32.5, 0:35.5), blue cards cut mid-word (0:41.0), a pale band along the left edge (0:50-0:51), a grey block where the next handwritten word will be (0:48.0).

late.what: Invert the time between the tricks and the essay (Idi's pinned note). Each of the eight prompts reads large for 1.5 s or more; the essay lands once per trick at stamp size; never two identical cards in one frame; the eight tricks do not share one four-step cycle.
late.basis: Idi's note; audit: essay family 0:58.2-1:09.1 = 10.9 s, prompts shown 0.9 s against 1.5 s needed; critic A dwell + repeat (high): twin cards at 0:59, 1:02, 1:04.5, 1:05, the same cycle four times.

late.what: No bubble under a card border and no card text cut mid-word by the frame (1:02.0, 1:02.5, 1:05.0, 1:07.5, 1:08.0).
late.basis: critic A stray x2 (med). Mostly falls out of late-e01.

late.what: The scale's readout holds a value long enough to read: today each TILT value lives 0.1 s. One settled value, or steps of 0.3 s or more.
late.basis: audit: micro TILT labels 0.1 s each, no cue; room dossier ref gap ("the small readout that explains the joke is hard to read").

late.what: Exits land on cues. First test of the film rule: of 7 in-place exits here 2 sit on a music cue and 4 have no cue of any kind.
KEPT: the gold star on the left against the lyric and the question mark on the right (0:53.5-0:55.5). The two pans are the picture.
late.basis: critic A two-focus (med), ruled by the lead.

chorus1.what: The title lands alone at 1:15.5: both handwriting lines, the rings and the pupil scene are still up when it arrives. They leave or dim first. Build with chorus1-s04 (the hand, Idi's MY WAY).
The curling column of script that hangs from the top edge at 1:17.0-1:18.5 leaves with the eye scene, or gets a cause.
Exits land on cues: 2 of 10 in-place exits sit on a music cue (chance 27 %).

fact.what: The tape section holds the sung line whole. At 1:32.0-1:35.0 the first lyric is cut by the left edge for 3 s while text sits in three places with chips, month marks and a bracket caption. Frame it, and stage the three text areas one after another.
The THEY diagram leaves or drops to texture one bar after it completes (done by 1:38, on screen to 1:43.5 under newer lines). One glowing question mark at a time (2 to 3 in a frame at 1:38-1:42).
fact.basis: critic A dwell (med), two-focus x2 (high), repeat (med).

fact.what: Edges, check at 30 fps: "built 'em too" cut by the bottom (1:35.0), three words cut by the bottom (1:41.5-1:42.0), the panel's bottom slice left in frame at the top (1:29.0), empty outline shapes at the top edge (1:38.0).

Stop drawing the WHAT DO YOU KNOW? card and its ANSWER and HINT chips when the hook ride leaves them. The engine draws them through all of games (34.4 s); the lead's eye at 2:10 finds them hidden. Seam item with games.
fact.basis: audit cross-plate texts; lead's eye on f_00131.

games.what: The dotted border changes with the level. It frames every picture for 34 s at one size and place, and the camera is still for 93 % of the plate.
games.basis: critic A dwell (high); camera probe (still 93 %, the film's highest).

games.what: The header tabs earn their stay or leave: INFINITE LIVES, GOD MODE ON, SPEEDRUNNERS sit 21-27 s after they are sung. Each tab changes state when its level ends (struck, greyed, counted) or leaves.
games.basis: audit dwell (6 words, to 2:18.6); critic A dwell (high); lead's eye at 2:10.

games.what: The trophies act on the line. They stand for 10.7 s (2:07.9-2:18.6, motionless 89-94 % of it) and the three *cheat enabled marks sit motionless for 6.8 s. One event per trophy, on the beat.
games.basis: audit dwell (trophy x3, fine x3); critic A dwell (high).

games.what: The upside-down VICTORY inset leaves when the speedrun line starts (unchanged 1:55.5-2:03.0).
games.basis: critic A dwell (med); audit: level, bars, victory 7.8 s, motionless 75-83 %.

games.what: Nothing on top of a sung line: the white label over AND EVERY LOBBY SEES YOUR STATS (2:07.5); three lyric lines cut on the left (2:03.0). Check HE on the border (1:47.0) and the garbled zoom frame (1:51.0) at 30 fps.
games.basis: critic A stray x4 (high, high, med, med).

games.what: `wall2` (65 % of the frame) leaves at 1:52.9 with no cue: move its exit onto the kick.
KEPT: the walls of ESSAY and WORK (1:51.5-1:52.0, about 60 copies for 1 s each). A wall of one word is the picture of the grind.
games.basis: audit repeat rows; critic A repeat (high), ruled by the lead.

chorus2.what: The opening's credit block scrolls off the receipt as the first chorus line prints. It rides for 10 s (2:18.6-2:28.7) and is a third reading of the same rows (open 2 s, here 10 s, outro 9 s).
The FREE to TWICE flip gets its own beat (today it lands in the frame where BILL YOU prints), and the TWICE tag reacts or leaves (unchanged 2:21.5-2:28.0).
The fractions sheet enters after the line lands and clear of the receipt: at 2:24-2:27 it is the brightest thing in frame while the lyric prints, with its title half hidden ("RACTIONS").

The wheel: the dark disc waits out of frame until its cue (it pokes in at 2:32.0 for 2.5 s), YOU at the hub reads whole and once (2:34-2:35), the empty ring leaves with its PAY ATTENTION token (it stays 4.5 s, 2:37.5-2:41.5).
The receipt prints in rhythm: `1 SKIP` (2:23.9) and `price?` (2:26.4) appear with no cue; 2 of 7 in-place entries sit on a music cue (chance 48 %).

kitchen.what: The five scene labels (IT'S LATE, ONE LAMP, THE KITCHEN TABLE, FRACTIONS, AND A TEST AT 8:00) stop being a list: each attaches to the thing it names and dims, or leaves once used. They sit unchanged for about 10 s while four quadrants move around them (2:52.5-2:55.0, the most crowded stretch of the second half).
kitchen.basis: critic B dwell (high), two-focus (high); audit: card words 8.6-11.0 s.

kitchen.what: Light and reading in one place at 3:05.0-3:13.5: the lamp flare is the largest, brightest thing for 9 s while all reading happens in small boxed rows beside it, in one framing for 18 frames; the line SO, WHAT'S A HALF OF A HALF stays 7.7-8.9 s after it is sung.
kitchen.basis: critic B two-focus + dwell (high); audit dwell (14 words; bars, clock, labels 11 s).

kitchen.what: The clock reads as a clock from its first frame: for 9 s (2:50-2:59) its segments read as the letters r:e.
Check at 30 fps: a blue table panel over the labels for one frame (2:56.5); the white receipt that is there for 4 frames and gone (2:53.5-2:55.0; `slip:bait` enters with no cue at 2:54.1).
kitchen.basis: critic B exit x2 (med); audit events.

kitchen.what: The lamp's pole runs through the typed line and the cursor (2:44.5-2:47.0) and through the IT'S LATE label (2:54); the handwritten TO THINK floats outside the screen attached to nothing (3:00.0-3:02.5).
kitchen.basis: critic B stray x2 (med); lead's eye on f_00175.

kitchen.what: The stacked trick bubbles cut each other's text mid-line (2:52-2:56: ASLEEP and two more lines show as half-letters under the next bubble). The newest bubble covers the older ones whole, or they fan apart. Build with the room item on the trick bubbles.
kitchen.basis: the PC's own model flagged the cut text 5 s in a row; lead's eye on f_00175.

exam.what: A QUARTER / NOW ASK ME WHY leaves on the solo's first kick. It holds for 12 s, the longest lyric hold in the film (median word stay here 8.7 s; film 2 s). Her three dots are the thread that stays. Build inside film-s02.
exam.basis: critic B dwell (high); audit dwell (4 words 8.3-9.1 s, herdots 11.2 s).

exam.what: The timer card and test header stand motionless for 6.6 s (87 % of it); the small clock enters at 3:17.1 and leaves at 3:20.9 with no cue. Both fold into the flip clock of film-s02.

verse4.what: One QUESTIONS and one 400 per frame at 3:34.5-3:36.0 (QUESTIONS twice, 400 three times; QUESTIONS ASKED up to 7 at once from 3:32.4).
verse4.basis: critic B repeat (high); audit repeat rows.

verse4.what: Calm the camera and keep type inside the frame: HUNDREDS DAILY cut in half by the top (3:33.0), the lyric block cut by the right edge (3:42.5), a holed grey bar at the frame edge (3:32.0), cards and hands cut by the bottom (3:54.5). This plate has the film's most camera reversals (41).
verse4.basis: critic B stray x4 (high, high, med, med); camera probe.

verse4.what: One focus at 3:48.5-3:54.0: seven kinds of thing in one frame at 3:53.5; four areas at 3:48.5 with the hand's wrist touching ANY QUESTIONS?.
The bulb-grid picture at 3:50.0-3:51.0 comes back unchanged in chorus 3 at 4:10.5. The second showing differs: more bulbs lit, a different framing. Seam item with chorus3.
Exits land on cues: 8 of 28 in-place exits sit on a music cue (chance 40 %). Counts toward film-s06.

chorus3.what: The callback list (1. THE THIRD TWENTY to 4. EIGHT HEADS) stops standing as a list for 12 s: a row lights when its picture returns and leaves when it has.
chorus3.basis: audit dwell strings (11.8-12.0 s each), family `list` 8.3 s.

chorus3.what: One PAY ATTENTION at a time: twice in a frame at 4:06.0-4:07.5 (background and card); four text layers with no gap at 4:08.0-4:09.5; a second small stack inside the giant lyric at 4:10.5.
The kitchen's five labels come back changed and clear of the lyric (4:12.5-4:15.5: unchanged, under a new three-line lyric, with the lamp flare touching line 1).
Type inside the frame: ATTENTION cut by the top (3:59.5, 4:05.5), THEN SOME MORE cut on the left (4:10.5), the lyric cut on the left (4:16.0).
chorus3.basis: critic B stray x4 (high, med, high, high).

chorus3.what: Strays, check at 30 fps: an empty black square mid-frame for 3.5 s (4:00-4:03), bright streaks from the top edge (4:00.0), a sliver of a pale panel behind the card (4:04-4:06).

outro.what: The stamp is the lyric: PAY ATTENTION, OR PAY THE PRICE is sung, shown as type and shown as a stamp at once, and the pair holds 9.5 s (4:28.5-4:37.5). One of the two carries the words.
outro.basis: critic B repeat (high), dwell (med); audit dwell (6 words 7.1-9.0 s; strip, box, coin 10.5-11.0 s).

outro.what: The receipt's recall reads: one tile per beat, each long enough to read or reduced to an icon, no type over type. Today four tiles live 1.1 s each and leave with no cue, THE ESSAY IS DEAD gets 1.0 s (needs 1.5), the essay line 0.3 s (needs 1.8), the blocks change every frame at 4:41.5-4:43.5 and FIVE prints over RECEIPT. Build with the room item on the trick bubbles.
outro.basis: audit reading rows x5, events x4; critic B two-focus (med), stray (med).

outro.what: The last line of the film is its easiest to read: CHANGE DUE and ONE QUESTION. print at the bottom edge at their smallest size after the zoom-out. Build inside film-s03.
Eye check: the PRICE row ends with no value while its four sibling rows have one (4:45.5-4:50.0). Fill it or make the gap the point.
The input bar is the widest thing in frame while the lyric being added is small (4:32-4:35): size follows what is being sung.

Edges and leftovers, check at 30 fps: the lyric cut by the left and bottom edges (4:37.0-4:37.5), WERE YOU EVER REALLY drawn over PRESENT at the seam (4:20.5), the dim leftover FIVE M / IN FUL cut on the right (4:45.5). Exits: 2 of 7 in-place exits on a music cue, 5 with no cue of any kind.
outro.basis: critic B stray x3 (high, med, med); audit events.
